$comment: Machine-readable form of the capability × surface table in docs/guides/choose.md. Hand-maintained, verified against the sources on the date below: library `call` names against docs/assets/api.json (the mechanically extracted export surface), CLI `command` names against packages.zipnative-cli.commandGroups and MCP `tool` names against packages.zipnative-mcp.tools in docs/assets/ecosystem.json (the single source of truth for names and counts — regenerate nothing from this file). All three surfaces are 1.0.0, so no `since` is recorded. `supported: false` cells carry a note naming the honest alternative where one exists.

library.notes: Lazy central-directory walk; nothing is decompressed.

cli.notes: text | json | ndjson; --long adds offsets, flags and extra fields; --include / --exclude globs.

mcp.notes: Paged (limit 200, max 2000); filter by names, prefix or globs; every row carries the sanitized path an extraction would use.

library.notes: No single report call — compose entries(), the diagnostics channel and verifyZip() yourself.

cli.notes: Eager open; repeatable --check assertions (deterministic, no-encryption, safe-names, max-entries=N, …) turn it into a CI gate — exit 1 / E_CHECK_FAILED.

mcp.notes: Same report shape as `zipnative inspect --json`; check[] and assert{} → checks[] + checksPassed.

library.notes: CRC-verified, zero-copy compressed source.

cli.notes: One or more entries to stdout or --output; --raw emits the compressed payload; CRC checked at end of stream like unzip -p.

mcp.notes: mode data | raw | verify; utf8 or base64 encoding; byte range; 16 MiB inline cap.

library.notes: Never throws for archive problems; structural refusals land in report.error.

cli.notes: Exit 1 / E_VERIFY_FAILED when not ok; --strict also fails on diagnostics; --entry restricts the scope.

mcp.notes: entries: all | failed | skipped | none keeps the response token-frugal.

library.notes: In memory only — returns data plus sanitized paths; the engine never writes files.

cli.notes: The filesystem trust boundary: zip-slip, symlink, duplicate, bomb and device-name guards on by default; --dry-run plans without writing; --skip-unsafe / --skip-unsupported opt into skipping.

mcp.notes: Inline base64 (32 MiB total) or outputMode: 'file' inside ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR with resource links; includeData: false is the dry run.

library.notes: Bounded memory, CRC verified, data-descriptor entries delimited by the resumable inflater. Trusts local headers alone.

cli.notes: stdin / pipes, no central directory; --list, --output-dir or --cat; every JSON output carries trust: 'local-headers-only'.

mcp.notes: Explicitly NOT authoritative; tolerateTruncation for damaged archives; data: none | verify | include.

library.notes: null for unsafe names — traversal, absolute, drive/UNC, NUL, ADS, Windows device names.

cli.notes: extract --dry-run reports what would be refused; inspect --check safe-names asserts it.

mcp.notes: Up to 10 000 names per call with a rejection reason each.

library.notes: compression: { deterministic: true } pins the pure-TS encoder — identical SHA-256 on every runtime; canonical order and DOS-epoch timestamps by default.

cli.notes: --deterministic, --order canonical | insertion (EPUB mimetype first), --date epoch | now | ISO, --from-manifest, --include / --exclude.

mcp.notes: Inline text / base64 or sandbox sourcePath entries; includeSha256 returns the digest with the archive.

library.notes: Byte-identical to createZip per compression tier; unconditional under deterministic: true.

cli.notes: --parallel with --workers, --min-job-size, --job-timeout; refused with --codec.

mcp.notes: parallel: { workers, minWorkerJobSize, jobTimeout }, capped by ZIPNATIVE_MCP_WORKERS.

library.notes: Data-descriptor layout; streamed entries ≤ 4 GiB (ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ZIP64_STREAMING beyond).

cli.notes: --stream writes with bounded memory; --stdin-name archives a pipe; --chunk-size tunes the writer.

mcp.notes: entries[].stream: true on a sandbox sourcePath feeds addStream; outputMode: 'file' assembles the archive by streaming to disk.

library.notes: save() is append-only (removed content stays recoverable); saveCompact() truly deletes. 7-Zip's CLI mis-reads append-only output.

cli.notes: --add / --replace / --remove / --rename / --comment; --compact for true deletion; --in-place with an atomic rename; every untouched entry is verified before re-emission.

mcp.notes: operations[] (add, replace, remove, rename, setComment); mode: append | compact.

library.notes: Seedable — continue a running checksum.

cli.notes: Files or stdin in 64 KiB chunks; --seed; --expect fails with E_CHECK_FAILED on mismatch.

mcp.notes: dataBase64, text or sandbox sourcePath; seed; expect.

library.notes: Resumable pure-TS inflater; reports exactly where the compressed stream ends.

cli.notes: --max-output bounds the expansion (default: the effective --max-entry-size, 1 GiB); --allow-trailing; --sync.

mcp.notes: maxOutput is REQUIRED; ZIP_INFLATE_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW when exceeded.

library.notes: The extension point for methods other than 0 and 8; deterministic: true refuses a foreign deflateImpl.

cli.notes: Executes user code — accepted on the command line only, never from .zipnativerc.json; batch manifests need --allow-codec-load.

mcp.notes: Deliberately not exposed: a codec module is arbitrary code. Methods 0 and 8 only (ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_METHOD otherwise).

library.call: limits option on openZip() / extractZip() / verifyZip() (DEFAULT_ZIP_LIMITS)
library.notes: Eight named bounds: entries, entry size, total size, ratio, name, extra-field, comment and central-directory bytes.

cli.notes: The same eight as global flags plus --max-input-size; 'none' disables one with a visible warning.

mcp.notes: Per-call limits are capped by the operator ceilings ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES / ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_ENTRIES (LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED above them).

library.call: onDiagnostic / strict on openZip() / extractZip() / verifyZip()
library.notes: Eleven diagnostic codes (prepended data, name mismatch, dead bytes, …) — recoverable findings, never thrown unless strict.

cli.notes: Diagnostics ride in the --json envelope; --strict turns the first one into a failure.

mcp.notes: Escalates the first diagnostic to ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC; otherwise diagnostics[] (de-duplicated, 200 kept) accompany the result.

library.notes: Which deflate tier (native, CompressionStream, pure-TS) the runtime will use.

cli.notes: Ten checks (node, engine, deflate tier, workers, codecs, limits, …) as text or --json; exit 1 on any failure.

mcp.notes: Engine version and tiers plus the server's caps, ceilings, sandbox and cache state.

library.notes: The mechanically extracted export surface and the frozen error registry; every thrown error carries a stable err.code.

cli.notes: 22 JSON Schema subjects (Draft 2020-12) incl. the capability manifest; --summary / --fields a,b.c project list, inspect, verify, stream and batch.

mcp.notes: verbosity: 'summary' and fields: […] project every read tool; _meta.examples ship executable inputs.

library.notes: Repository-level policy: .github/ai-governance.json and npm run verify:issue for issue drafts.

cli.notes: govern rules | policy | verify-issue <draft.md> — E_POLICY on violation.

mcp.notes: Drafts a compliant issue (never files it); the governance_contract and draft_issue_workflow prompts explain the rules.

library.notes: By design — the engine never touches the filesystem; extraction returns data plus sanitized paths.

cli.notes: The CLI is the trust boundary: --output-dir, --output, --in-place; refuses to overwrite without --overwrite.

mcp.notes: Only inside ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR (the one sandbox); results are exposed as zipnative://output/{+path} resources.

library.notes: Compose the calls in your own code — recipes/ shows the patterns.

cli.notes: Directory mode (--input-dir, --task create | verify, --concurrency) or manifest mode (ten whitelisted commands, @id output references, one JSON report on stdout).

mcp.notes: One call per tool; the host orchestrates. Results can be chained through the sandbox (outputPath → zipPath).

cli.notes: bash | zsh | fish | powershell, generated from the same command table as --help.

library.notes: By policy in 1.x — ZipCrypto is broken. Encrypted entries are detected (entry.isEncrypted) and reads throw ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION. Delegate confidentiality to the document layer (pdfnative AES-256, Office) and archive the encrypted files — use-cases guide, Case 5.

cli.notes: Encrypted entries are listed, skipped by verify, refused by extract unless --skip-unsupported; inspect --check no-encryption asserts their absence.

mcp.notes: There is no password input; verify_zip skips encrypted entries, extract_zip refuses them; modify_zip can still copy them untouched.
